test(types): exhaustively pin every field's exact Rust type and every type's derive list across the full SPEC-006 cluster (AC-001, AC-005, AC-009, AC-010, AC-012, AC-015)

serde treats several distinct Rust types identically on the wire (String vs camino::Utf8PathBuf, f64 vs another float width, usize vs another integer width), so only a compile-time `let x: ExactType = value.field` binding can distinguish the declared field type from a serde-equivalent sibling -- not a runtime assertion. This test inventories and pins all 21 fields across CodeBlock (8), ParentContext (3), RankedBlock (7), and Diagnostic (3) in one place (LineHit's own 2 fields are pinned separately in T-021, for 23 fields across the full six-type cluster), plus each type's derive list via generic bound-check functions -- assert_full_derives and assert_enum_derives now additionally bound Serialize + DeserializeOwned, not just Debug + Clone, so this test proves CodeBlock/Diagnostic/DiagnosticKind actually satisfy their full declared derive lists -- so completeness is self-evident without cross-referencing types.rs by hand and without relying on later gate rounds to find gaps piecemeal -- the exact lesson PLAN-005's 6 gate-and-fix cycles established.

tasks.commit_message:
test(types): pin RankedBlock's and ParentContext's absence of Deserialize, and LineHit's absence of both Serialize and Deserialize, via a const-based specialization probe (AC-005, AC-009, AC-015)

A positive generic bound check (T-022's assert_full_derives/assert_serialize_only_derives) can only prove a trait IS implemented, never that it is absent -- the compile-time proof for absence instead relies on inherent-impl-over-trait-default priority: SerProbe<T>/DeProbe<T>'s const IS resolves to true only when a narrower inherent impl bounded by Serialize/DeserializeOwned actually applies to T, and falls back to a trait-provided false otherwise. Positive controls (RankedBlock's own Serialize, CodeBlock's and Diagnostic's own Deserialize) confirm the probe itself is not just always false.
